correction.text: the Wajinchi, the Wajin territory on the southern Oshima Peninsula around Matsumae and Esashi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: a domain inside the Tokugawa realm that Cliopatria draws only inside Warring States Japan and the Tokugawa Shogunate. The Matsumae clan page: Hideyoshi 'gave the Matsumae the area around what is now Matsumae, Hokkaidō as a march fief in 1590'; the Matsumae Domain page: 'the Wajin territory on the Oshima Peninsula (Wajinchi), with the rest of Ezo as Ezochi'; the History of Hokkaido page: the Matsumae 'governed southern Ezochi until the end of the Edo period'. About 5,600 km2 for the southern Oshima Peninsula by the gazetteer (a polygon, no page gives a boundary or an area). The Ezochi relation is a vassal tint in the ledger; the 1799-1821 shogunate takeover of eastern Ezo is no page's, see the ledger.

ledger.note: 1590: Hideyoshi makes Matsumae a march fief. He 'gave the Matsumae the area around what is now Matsumae, Hokkaidō as a march fief in 1590'; infobox 'Established 1590', Matsumae Yoshihiro's tenure 1590-1616. The page gives a place, not a boundary; the Wajinchi polygon is the researcher's reading.

minus.text: the Wajinchi, the Wajin territory on the southern Oshima Peninsula around Matsumae and Esashi

ledger.note: 1669: Shakushain's revolt. 'In 1669, the revolt began as a fight for resources between Shakushain's people and another Ainu clan led by Hae' in the Shibuchari basin; the Ainu then 'aimed to capture the colonial cities in the Matsumae Domain' and attacked Yamato people, ships, mining camps and trading forts across Hokkaido.

minus.text: the Wajinchi, the Wajin territory on the southern Oshima Peninsula around Matsumae and Esashi

ledger.note: 1672: the revolt is put down. Infobox '1669 to 1672', 'Japanese victory'; the Matsumae clan page: 'Shakushain's revolt was finally put down' in 1672; Shakushain's forces had surrendered at the end of 1669.

minus.text: the Wajinchi, the Wajin territory on the southern Oshima Peninsula around Matsumae and Esashi

ledger.note: 1672: the Ainu swear allegiance. 'The peace treaty required the Ainu to swear allegiance to Matsumae', yet 'The Ainu tribes remained autonomous' and Matsumae set up 60 trading posts; the Matsumae Domain page already gives the clan 'the authority to govern over Ezo' in 1599 and exclusive trading rights in 1604 (Ieyasu's black seal), the History of Hokkaido page the 'exclusive trading rights with the Ainu'. A tint, not annexation.

region.text: eastern Ezo, as Cliopatria's Tokugawa shape adds it in 1799

ledger.note: 1799: the shogunate takes eastern Ezo (mirror of tokugawa-shogunate's 1799 gain). The Ainu people page: '1799-1806: The Tokugawa shogunate took direct control of southern Hokkaido'; the Hakodate bugyō page has 'In 1779, the Tokugawa shogunate exerted direct control over Hakodate' and 'The office was created in 1802'; the Matsumae Domain page says 'the shogunate often assumed control over Ezo' in the late Edo period. The land is Cliopatria's Tokugawa 1799 addition (researcher's reading of the page's region); no opened page dates the 1807 step or the Matsumae's removal.

region.text: eastern Ezo, as Cliopatria's Tokugawa shape adds it in 1799

ledger.note: 1822: eastern Ezo returns to the Matsumae (mirror of tokugawa-shogunate's 1822 loss). Page silent on the date and the return; bridged from the end of Cliopatria's 1799-1821 shape (confidence 1).

minus.text: the Wajinchi, the Wajin territory on the southern Oshima Peninsula around Matsumae and Esashi

ledger.note: 1855: the shogunate takes Ezochi. After the Treaty of Shimoda defined the Russo-Japanese border, 'Tokugawa control (1855-1858): The shogunate took over control of most of Ezochi'; the Matsumae keep the Wajinchi.

1868: the seat moves from Matsumae Castle to Tate Castle in Assabu. 'The castle was relocated to Tatejo in Assabu-cho and became Tatehan'; the Matsumae had allied with the Ōu-Etsu alliance and the Seigi-tai defected to the new government and moved to Tate Castle.
18 December 1868: Matsumae Castle falls to Enomoto's republic. 'December 18, 1868: Matsumae Castle was captured'; the fleet had reached Hakodate on 3 December and taken it about 8 December.
28 December 1868: Esashi falls; 'End of 1868: The rebels held the whole region' (Republic of Ezo page). The rest of the Wajinchi, from Hakodate to Kumaishi, goes with it (researcher's reading).

region.text: the Wajinchi, the Wajin territory on the southern Oshima Peninsula around Matsumae and Esashi

ledger.note: June 1869: the Matsumae regain their land. The Republic ended on 27 June 1869 (Goryōkaku handed to Kuroda Kiyotaka); on 24 June 1869 'Matsumae Nobuhiro's request to reinstate the domain name was approved, and he became its governor' (Matsumae Domain page).

The Matsumae Domain page has 'transformed into a prefecture on July 14, 1871', which is the Japanese-calendar date (Meiji 4, 7th month, 14th day); the Abolition of the han system page gives 'In August 1871 ... forced through an Imperial Edict' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolition_of_the_han_system); infobox 'Disestablished 1871'. notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from five pages (Matsumae Domain, Matsumae clan, Shakushain's revolt, Hakodate bugyō, History of Hokkaido) plus the Republic of Ezo page for 1868-1869. The han is an internal unit of the Tokugawa realm; Cliopatria draws Ezo only in Warring States Japan (from 1552, southern Oshima) and the Tokugawa Shogunate (eastern Ezo 1799-1821, most of Hokkaido from 1856). The Wajinchi boundary and the 1799/1807/1821 shogunate takeover are on no opened page (the Ainu people page dates '1799-1806' direct control of southern Hokkaido and '1807' Japan's claim on Sakhalin, which the ainu dossier uses): the 1822 return of eastern Ezo is a confidence-1 mirror of the sister tokugawa-shogunate dossier and the 1799 takeover (confidence 2) takes its year from the Ainu people page; their counterpart is 'nobody' there and 'ainu' here; the vassal_end/vassal_start pair covers eastern Ezo only, a partial end of the Ezochi tint (the ainu slug is the counterpart of the tint; an ainu dossier is written by this batch). Disagreements: Matsumae Domain page says 1869 governor Nobuhiro while its list has Nagahiro 1869-1871; its list repeats the names Yoshihiro and Norihiro. The Republic of Ezo's proclamation was 27 January 1869 and its end 26-27 June 1869 (Republic of Ezo page); the empire-of-japan dossier ends its contest and records the gain in May 1869 and the tokugawa-shogunate dossier June 1869. Kokudaka: 10,000 koku from 1719 (before that guest vassal, then hatamoto), 30,000 koku from 1765; the 70,000-koku figure on the page is the trade revenue. Sakhalin: an anajinya at Kusharukotan from 1679 (fishing hub), not drawn. Gazetteer: no 'Matsumae' or 'Esashi' place (coordinate circles used); Wajinchi is a polygon intersected with Hokkaido. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
